difficultyRationale: Requires knowing that Java maintains category-specific default locales for display text and formatting.
prompt: Which statements about `Locale.Category` are correct? Select all that apply.
explanation: Java defines separate default-locale categories. `DISPLAY` is used for user-interface display information, while `FORMAT` is used for formatting dates, numbers, and similar locale-sensitive data.

options.text: Locale.Category.DISPLAY is associated with display-oriented locale data.
options.explanation: It is the category for user-interface display information.

options.text: Locale.Category.FORMAT is associated with locale-sensitive formatting.
options.explanation: It is used by formatting-oriented APIs.

options.text: Java has only one default Locale and no category-specific defaults.
options.explanation: Category-specific defaults are part of the Locale API.

options.text: FORMAT controls module readability in JPMS.
options.explanation: Locale categories are unrelated to the module system.
